questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted a cultural experience that was different than that of Denmark/European countries/English speaking countries. Going on exchange to Taiwan seemed like a very unique opportunity to live in Taipei and experience a very different and interesting part of the world. And since I was doing my exchange in the fall semester I also looked for a place with nicer weather than the danish fall and Taiwan seemed perfect in that sense as well.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think my time in Taiwan was pretty amazing. I think Taipei is a really cool city to live in and Taiwan is a beautiful contry with very kind people and it is easy to explore and experience due to its small size. The only reason I won't give it a 10 is because the whole process leading up to the exchange was quite tedious and KU is slightly incompetent in some aspects.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was alright I think. When I arrived I had to do 7 days quarantine in a hotel room so I could do some of the course application stuff there.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got mails from NTU both before and after arrival. I lot of it seemed a bit last minute but a lot of the deadlines were very close to semester start so it all worked out fine. They also have NTU online and some other site where information is available.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: NTU recommended the website: MyRoomAbroad to look for off campus housing so I found something there a month or two prior to arrival. The website was pretty easy to use but I got quite a few rejections before getting something so might want to start in good time and be patient.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in a shared flat at the Shida night market which is quite close to NTU and right next to another large university called NTNU so the area is young and lively. The biggest dormitory for exchange students is the Prince House Dorms, which is located just south of NTU in the Gonguan area. This area is also very nice and a lot of exchange students will be living there so if you are getting housing on your own i would recommend looking for something in this area or in the Shida area (the area I lived in hehe) since it is close to both uni and the dorms. There are also nice areas north of campus but I wouldn't recommend going much more north than Da'an Park. There are also other dorm options that are further from campus but thats a bit wack I think (but cheap!!).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't get a place at the dorms even though I applied (Mostly scholarship students seemed to get it) but I was very happy with my place.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember the details sorry. There are 2 stages which are specific time slots (like 2 day periods or something) pretty close to semester start where you can register for courses. The strategy is to just register for a bunch of courses and then you can deregister them later all the way until 2 weeks into to semester start. If you don't get some of the courses that you want, you can show up in class during the first 2 weeks and talk to the professor and usually you will get a spot.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Everyone were assigned a student volunteer, a local student that can help answer your questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I ended up getting everything I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just apply for a bunch in the 2 online registration stages and deregister later if necessary. And during the first 2 weeks of semester go to the classes you want and ask the professor after class for a registration code.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was very varied. Some were super easy didn't really feel like university level and some were quite difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is different in the sense that they have homework and quizzes and midterms which are part of your final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Forest Climate & Practice - Forestry Department
Principles of Remote Sensing - Geography Department
Climate and Ocean: From Past to Future - Oceanography Department
Exploring Taiwan: natural environment and resources - Don't remember if it was a specific department but it was very easy and mainly aimed at exchange students.
Forest Ecosystem Flux - Forestry Department
Introduction to Field Geology (II) - Department of Geosciences I think

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All "Exploring Taiwan" courses are pretty easy and chill and aimed at exchange students but academically not very interesting.
I enjoyed the Forest climate and practice and the climate and ocean courses, they were pretty interesting and not too hard not super easy.
The Field geology course was nice since there was a weekend long field trip where you get to see the southern part of the island, and the course only consists of 1 indoor class, the field trip and then the final exam so it frees up your schedule a bit. But the indoor class and the final exam were both on saturdays so that is a bit annoying.
I didn't really like the teaching style in the remote sensing course. There are quizzes every week that count towards your final grade and they are based on the lecture. But there is no additional litterature available so if the slides arn't enough then you are kind of lost. Only the last 3 or 4 weeks are practical remote sensing where you actually do stuff at a computer and they teach Google Earth Engine where you need to code to use it and since ive never done any coding before it was a bit rough at times.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Spend a fortune on a pair of hiking pants but I love it

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is stupid cheap, beers at bars is basically the same as DK maybe a bit cheaper if you find the right places.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined the NTU table tennis club and played with the Gepgraphy department team as well and it was pretty fun. All the departments have sports teams in all kinds of different sports you just have to ask local class mates and they can probably tell you when and where. There is a sports center on campus with a bunch of facilities. I used the gym and played squash with friends sometimes but you have to pay.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a lot of student clubs and you can find a list online somewhere and there is also some club fare stuff at the start of the semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do whatever you like.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The island is perfect for going on weekend trips or day trips. For day trips I think its nice to visit places in the north like Tamsui, Yelihu Geopark, Jiufen, Yangmingshan, going to the beach, hotsprings, taking the gondola close to the zoo, or whatever you find interesting. For weekends you can get around the island by Train and visist different cities. For the east coast the TRA is wonderful and for the west coast the high speed rail is very convinient.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The language is a bit of a barrier and can make simple tasks like ordering food a bit of a challenge but it is completely fine and the people are super friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The english level of the local students is typically not that good which makes it hard to make real friends with locals but i think the best way for me was thorugh department table tennis and table tennis club.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Don't recall anything super challenging except for the language being impossible.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The country feels super safe, noone steals, everyone is kind and respectful and the taiwanese food is amazing.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get a place close to campus and the Prince House Dorms.
Go on weekend and day trips.
Sign up for general chinese course in the evening since there are a lot of exchange students and you can drink beer afterwards. I dropped out of the course after a month but I could still continue the beer drinking part of the evening.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Probably but I'm not sure what but good luck.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: So many new experiences and new people and in the end I think I got everything I wanted out of my exchange adventure.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The final exam week my PC broke down and I got sick with the shingles but it wasn't too bad.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Wup!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
